name: Booking platform (demo)
description: An invented, generic booking system used to demonstrate codefloor: web and admin clients, an API gateway, five services, shared data stores and two third-party providers.

nodes.label: Web app
nodes.description: Customer-facing single-page app for searching dates, booking and managing reservations. Talks only to the API gateway over HTTPS.

nodes.label: Admin console
nodes.description: Staff UI for managing properties, prices and manual refunds. Uses the same gateway with an admin role.

nodes.label: Mobile app
nodes.description: Native iOS/Android client reusing the public gateway API. Planned after the web launch.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.description: Single public entry point. Terminates TLS, verifies session tokens with the auth service, rate-limits, and routes requests to internal services.

nodes.label: Auth service
nodes.description: Issues and verifies session tokens. Stores users and hashed credentials in Postgres.

nodes.label: Availability service
nodes.description: Answers "what is free for these dates" queries. Reads inventory from Postgres and caches hot searches in Redis for 60 seconds.

nodes.label: Booking service
nodes.description: Owns the booking lifecycle (pending, confirmed, cancelled). Places a short-lived inventory hold, then confirms when a payment.succeeded event arrives.

nodes.label: Payments service
nodes.description: Creates payment intents and refunds with the payment provider, verifies its webhooks and publishes payment events. Never stores card data.

nodes.label: Notifications service
nodes.description: Consumes booking events and sends confirmation and cancellation emails through the email provider.

nodes.label: Waitlist service
nodes.description: Will let customers join a waitlist for sold-out dates and notify them when a cancellation frees a slot.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.description: Primary relational store for users, inventory, bookings and payment records. One schema per service.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.description: Search cache and short-lived inventory holds, both TTL based.

nodes.label: Event bus
nodes.description: Durable topic for domain events (payment.succeeded, booking.confirmed, booking.cancelled) with at-least-once delivery.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.description: Third-party card processor. Receives payment intents and refunds, and calls back through a signed webhook.

nodes.label: Email provider
nodes.description: Transactional email API used for confirmations and receipts.

flows.name: Search availability
flows.description: A customer looks for free dates; hot searches are served from cache.

steps.label: Pick dates
steps.detail: The customer enters a date range and guest count.

steps.label: Route search
steps.detail: The gateway rate-limits and forwards the query.

steps.label: Check cache
steps.detail: The service looks up the search key in Redis.

steps.label: Cache miss
steps.detail: No cached result, so the service falls back to the database.

steps.label: Read inventory
steps.detail: Free units for the range are computed from inventory rows.

steps.label: Cache and return
steps.detail: The result is cached for 60 seconds and returned.

steps.label: Render results
steps.detail: Available options are listed with prices.

flows.name: Create booking
flows.description: From clicking Book to a pending booking with a payment intent.

steps.label: Submit booking
steps.detail: The customer confirms dates and guest details.

steps.label: Verify session
steps.detail: The gateway asks the auth service to validate the token.

steps.label: Validate token
steps.detail: The token signature and expiry are checked.

steps.label: Create pending booking
steps.detail: A booking is created in the pending state.

steps.label: Hold inventory
steps.detail: The units are held for 10 minutes so nobody else can take them.

steps.label: Save booking
steps.detail: The pending booking row is written.

steps.label: Create payment intent
steps.detail: The booking service asks payments for an intent.

steps.label: Collect card
steps.detail: The customer completes payment on the provider's hosted form.

flows.name: Payment confirmation
flows.description: The provider's webhook turns a pending booking into a confirmed one and emails the customer.

steps.label: Send webhook
steps.detail: The provider calls back with a signed payment result.

steps.label: Route webhook
steps.detail: The public webhook path is forwarded to payments.

steps.label: Verify signature
steps.detail: The signature is checked before anything is trusted.

steps.label: Record payment
steps.detail: The payment record is stored for reconciliation.

steps.label: Publish payment.succeeded
steps.detail: Payments emits the event; it does not call booking directly.

steps.label: Confirm booking
steps.detail: The booking moves to confirmed and the hold is released.

steps.label: Publish booking.confirmed
steps.detail: Downstream consumers learn about the confirmation.

steps.label: Build email
steps.detail: The confirmation email is rendered from a template.

steps.label: Send email
steps.detail: The email is delivered to the customer.

flows.name: Cancel with refund
flows.description: A customer cancels; inventory is released and the card is refunded.

steps.label: Cancel booking
steps.detail: The customer cancels from their reservations page.

steps.label: Route request
steps.detail: The authenticated request goes to the booking service.

steps.label: Mark cancelled
steps.detail: The booking is cancelled and its units freed.

steps.label: Release inventory
steps.detail: Inventory rows are updated in the same transaction.

steps.label: Request refund
steps.detail: Booking asks payments to refund the captured amount.

steps.label: Refund card
steps.detail: The provider refunds the original payment method.

steps.label: Publish booking.cancelled
steps.detail: Consumers are told the booking is gone.

steps.label: Send cancellation
steps.detail: A cancellation email with the refund amount is prepared.

steps.label: Deliver email
steps.detail: The customer receives the cancellation notice.
